text:
maria: FYI noticed a spike of spot terminations in us-west-2 around 03:10. Thinking we should prototype an active "migrate-on-risk" flow for long-running in-flight requests to avoid repeat wasted compute.
derek: How do you detect "risk"? We get provider IMPENDING_TERMINATION hook but it's only 2 mins. Any earlier signal?
maria: telemetry has evict_score (0-1) predicting term within next N seconds. Not perfect but gives lead time.
toni: Key constraints: cost and safety. If we move work to reserved, we double-account unless we tag and attribute. Also reserved capacity can saturate quickly.
sam: What about a two-tier move: (1) transfer context to a warm prewarmed worker (cheap), (2) if warm not available, fallback to full reserved slot. Warm transfer should be fast and cheaper.
derek: Agree. For decision we need a simple expected-value rule: if evict_p * expected_remaining_cost_of_redo > cost_of_migration then migrate. expected_remaining_cost = tokens_left * cost_per_token + latency_penalty.
toni: We also need admission caps: per-tenant burst_credits + global migrations_per_minute limit. Prevent thundering migration floods.
maria: Implementation sketch: control-plane periodically scores in-flight requests and emits Recommendation objects. Operator consumes recs, revalidates admission, then executes migration. Keep operator idempotent/stateless.
sam: Example Recommendation proto (concept):
```
{
 "req_id": "r-0a1b",
 "action": "suggest_migrate",
 "score": "0.82",
 "ttl_s": "45",
 "why": "evict_score high; eta 180s"
}
```
derek: TTL is important so operator doesn't act on stale recs. Also add rec_version so we can reconcile conflicting recs.
toni: Observability: track metrics migrations_triggered, migrations_blocked_by_admission, post_migration_p95_latency, migration_cost_delta, tenant_charge_tags. Traces must link original -> migrated request.
maria: Rollout plan: stage 1: enable for a tiny internal tenant set with feature_flag=spot_migrate_alpha; stage 2: canary 5% of burst-eligible tenants; stage 3: expand based on cost/latency.
sam: Circuit breaker ideas: disable automatically if weekly reserved spend delta > 4% or migration_error_rate > 5% for two consecutive days.
derek: Add a per-request cooldown (don't re-migrate same request within 10m) and a per-tenant migration-rate limiter.
toni: For testing, we should build a sim harness: feed in traces, inject evict sequences (Poisson or bernoulli), simulate warm pool sizes and costs, compute net delta. Use that to tune thresholds instead of guessing.
maria: Also need billing plumbing: mark migrated tokens as migrated=true so reports don't double-count. Reconciliation job for any orphaned charges.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: rollout plan queued -> feature_flag=spot_migrate_alpha target=canary 10%
sam: Who owns the RFC and rollout? I'd propose runtime team owns control-plane scoring RFC, infra owns operator execution plumbing, billing owns tagging.
derek: Sounds right. I'll open the RFC draft with decision function pseudocode, sim notes, and rollout checklist.
maria: Great. I'll add a short proposal for warm-transfer protocol (how to snapshot KV-cache and resume).
toni: One last note: prefer conservative thresholds early. False-migrations are noisy but safer than dropping user work; cost can be tuned.
maria: Cool. I'll ping when the RFC is up. Thanks!
